cards.explanation: The answer is their own sins. The LORD says, "…you were sold for your iniquities, and for your transgressions your mother was sent away." He names their own sins as the reason. I think that's a hard line to hear, friends, but He says it plainly.

The answer is False. The LORD asks if His hand is too short and if He lacks the strength to deliver. Then He answers with a show of power: "Behold, My rebuke dries up the sea; I turn the rivers into a desert…" So those questions aren't a confession, friends. Nothing in these verses says His strength has run out.
The answer is that His rebuke dries up the sea. He says, "…My rebuke dries up the sea…" One rebuke and a whole sea is dry, friends. That's the power He's pointing to.

The answer is True. The LORD says, "I clothe the heavens in black and make sackcloth their covering." The sea is dry, the rivers are desert, and now the sky is dressed in black. He just keeps going, friends.

The answer is that He awakens the speaker's ear to listen. The speaker says, "He awakens Me morning by morning; He awakens My ear to listen as a disciple." Morning after morning, the ear gets woken up to listen. You know how people hit the snooze button about every round, friends? Nobody's proud of that.

The answer is True. The speaker says, "The Lord GOD has opened My ears, and I have not been rebellious, nor have I turned back." Ears open, no rebellion, no turning back, friends. All three go together in that one verse.

The answer is False. The speaker says, "I did not hide My face from scorn and spittle." Verse 6 is a heavy one, friends, with strikes and a torn-out beard. I think it's worth noticing that He doesn't hide His face.
The answer is flint. The speaker says, "…I have set My face like flint…" Flint is a hard stone, so it's a picture of a face that won't budge, friends. He says it because the Lord GOD helps Him.

The answer is that He is near. The speaker says, "The One who vindicates Me is near." Then comes the challenge, "Who will dare to contend with Me?" The nearness comes first, friends, and then the questions.

The answer is garment. The speaker says, "…they will all wear out like a garment; the moths will devour them." It's a picture of something wearing out, friends. It comes right after the speaker asks, "Who is there to condemn Me?"

The answer is to trust the LORD's name. The verse says, "Let him trust in the name of the LORD; let him lean on his God." The person in the dark with no light is told to trust and to lean, friends. Those are the two things the verse says.

The answer is a place of torment. The verse says, "You will lie down in a place of torment." This one is heavy, friends. It's spoken to those who kindle a fire and array themselves with firebrands, and who are told to walk in the light of their fire.
